title: SWPC ALTK08: K-index of 8 Reached (G4 - Severe)

fields.headline: Geomagnetic K-index of 8

potentialImpacts.heading: Area of Impact
potentialImpacts.text: Primarily poleward of 45 degrees Geomagnetic Latitude.

potentialImpacts.heading: Induced Currents
potentialImpacts.text: Possible widespread voltage control problems, and some protective systems may mistakenly trip out key assets from the grid.

potentialImpacts.heading: Spacecraft
potentialImpacts.text: Systems may experience surface charging; increased drag on low Earth-orbit satellites and orientation problems may occur.

potentialImpacts.heading: Navigation
potentialImpacts.text: Satellite navigation (GPS) degraded or inoperable for hours.

potentialImpacts.heading: Radio
potentialImpacts.text: HF (high frequency) radio propagation sporadic or blacked out.

potentialImpacts.heading: Aurora
potentialImpacts.text: Aurora may be seen as low as Alabama and northern California.

fields.footer: *** EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE *** Exercise product. Not an official NOAA message.

instructorNote: Hand this out at 15:10 CDT with the WARK08 from 14:40 (Serial 0158, valid 1940Z to 0300Z, Onset). Then read out the analyst's chat (two TOPs above their thresholds, "Do we go to Emergency? The clock runs out at 2025Z"), the EMS readings (Iron Range AT2 134 A and Hartley AT1 109 A, both rising) and the North Shore GPS caution (satellites tracked 11 → 7, signal strength (C/N0) down 6 dB, still LOCKED). Watch for the RCSM to declare Emergency by 15:25 with 30-minute calls and notice to the state, the CRSS to declare Condition 4 and start the clock for notifying entities, the RE to track the 150 A trigger, and TIME to tell the CRSS before acting on the clock.
